primitives.name: Gender-Aware DLS Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Proposed method: DLS-Cal, a 4-layer MLP (widths [18,128,128,64,1], GELU, dropout 0.25, 27,265 params, final layer zero-initialized) trained on Huber loss (δ=10) with AdamW (η=1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 512, cosine annealing, ≤50 epochs, patience 8) to predict the DLS residual r - r̂DLS.
primitives.assumptions: Gender differences in match dynamics exist; separate models improve fairness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In presence of significant gender bias in historical data.

layer2.mapping: GSE incorporates gender stratification into calibration kernel; enables fairer probabilistic forecasting.

primitives.name: Format-Specific Bias Audit
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is the first large-scale empirical audit of DLS as deployed (8,150 international matches), with a gender-differential fairness finding that the author states has not previously been documented.
primitives.assumptions: Bias varies by format (ODI/T20I) and gender; empirical audit identifies discrepancies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When format-specific DLS parameters fail to generalize.

layer2.mapping: GSE audits format-specific biases in probabilistic forecasts; aligns with DLS audit framework.
layer2.telemetry: ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis test statistics on format-specific residuals.

reasoning_traces.think:
The DLS method computes revised targets based on resource fractions consumed. The audit reveals systematic bias in its application across formats and genders. The proposed DLS-Cal model corrects this via a neural network predicting the residual difference between actual and DLS-predicted runs. This correction is applied as a state-conditioned residual adjustment, enabling interpretability and fairness. The calibration layer uses a 4-layer MLP trained with Huber loss and AdamW optimizer. It operates on a feature vector including DLS prediction, bucket bias, and enriched match features. The Win-Flip Rate (WFR) serves as a proxy for outcome reliability, indicating when predictions flip outcomes. The method's core insight is that DLS alone fails to capture dynamic match conditions, necessitating a residual-based correction layer. The gender-aware variant separates models to mitigate observed disparities. The audit validates that DLS residuals exhibit significant format and gender variance, which the calibration layer addresses. The failure mode occurs when static DLS parameters do not reflect evolving match dynamics or systemic biases.
